Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex EV Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question during this time, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. If you're using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex EV's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Taylor Kim, Chief Manufacturing Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q3 2024 was a strong quarter for Apex EV. We delivered 152,347 vehicles globally, up 28% year-over-year and 12% sequentially, putting us on pace for full-year guidance of 650,000 to 700,000 units. We made significant progress in several key areas, including ramping production toward a 500,000 annual run rate by year-end 2025 through vertical integration and supply chain resilience, launching an affordable product pipeline like the Apex C1 compact crossover with strong pre-orders, expanding geographically into Europe and Asia-Pacific to diversify beyond North America, advancing technology leadership in batteries, software, and sustainability, and executing cost reduction initiatives that expanded gross margins to 24.8%. The demand for our Apex X mid-size SUV and Apex T pickup continues to be strong, and we are working diligently to increase production capacity to meet that demand, with our new models exceeding initial expectations on range, pricing, and adoption.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. For Q3 2024, our revenue was $6.2 billion, representing a 35% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 24.8%, reflecting our ongoing efforts to improve operational efficiency through vertical integration and scale. Our operating expenses were $1.1 billion, and net income was $850 million. We continue to maintain a healthy balance sheet with $4.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Our guidance for the next quarter is revenue of $2.55 billion to $2.75 billion and deliveries of 170,000 to 185,000 units.

Let me kick things off with our core operational metric: total vehicle deliveries. In Q3, Apex EV delivered 152,347 vehicles globally, marking a robust 28% year-over-year increase from 118,900 units in Q3 2023, and a solid 12% sequential growth from 136,200 units in Q2 2024. This brings our year-to-date deliveries to 458,920 units, putting us on track to exceed our full-year guidance of 650,000 to 700,000 units, assuming no major macroeconomic disruptions.

Breaking it down by model lineup, our diversified portfolio continues to drive outsized growth. Our flagship Apex X mid-size SUV, accounting for 52% of total deliveries at 79,300 units, surged 35% year-over-year thanks to the recent rollout of our Gen 3 Long Range variant with LFP battery packs sourced from our new Nevada gigafactory partnership with CATL. This model achieved a class-leading 520-mile EPA range, undercutting competitors by 5% on price while matching efficiency at 3.2 mi/kWh. Close behind, the Apex S sedan delivered 45,620 units, or 30% of mix, up 22% year-over-year, fueled by strong fleet sales to Uber and Lyft under our Ride-Hail Optimized program, which includes over-the-air updates for Level 3 autonomy via our ApexMind ADAS stack.

Our heavy-duty Apex T pickup, now in full production ramp at our Texas Gigafactory, contributed 27,427 units, or 18% of mix—a staggering 85% year-over-year jump from early pilot builds last year. This positions us neck-and-neck with rivals in the U.S. full-size EV truck segment, where we've captured 12% market share year-to-date. Rounding out the portfolio, our new entry-level Apex Mini urban crossover notched first-quarter deliveries of 5,400 units post-launch in late Q2, validating our push into the sub-$35,000 segment to compete directly and capture IRA tax credit beneficiaries.

Regionally, North America led with 92,450 units, or 61% of total, up 32% year-over-year, driven by IRA-compliant production localization—now 85% U.S.-sourced content—and pent-up demand post-summer rate cuts. Inventory levels remain healthy at 18,000 units, with days' supply at 22 days versus the industry's 45-day average. Europe delivered 30,500 units, or 20%, flat year-over-year amid softening demand from subsidy phase-outs, but we gained 2 points of EV market share to 4.1%, thanks to our Berlin-assembled Apex X RWD qualifying for eco-bonuses. Asia-Pacific saw 21,200 units, or 14%, up 15% year-over-year despite competition; our Shanghai JV with BAIC ramped to 15,000 units per month, offsetting tariffs on Chinese cells. Emerging markets like Australia and Latin America added 8,200 units, or 5%, led by Apex Mini exports.

Key trends include our supply chain resilience: Q3 production hit 158,000 units at 98% OEE, mitigating chip shortages via dual-sourcing with TSMC and Samsung for our cylindrical cells. Gross margins on deliveries expanded 450 basis points year-over-year to 24.8%, reflecting scale and a mix shift toward higher-ASP trucks at $68,000 average over sedans at $42,000. We navigated headwinds like softer China retail demand and stabilizing U.S. lease penetration at 28%.

Strategically, we're accelerating vertical integration with 20 GWh of in-house cell production online by year-end, targeting 30% cost reductions. Our software ecosystem differentiates us: 65% of Q3 deliveries included ApexMind Highway Autonomy subscriptions at $199 per month ARPU, with 42% attachment rates. Q4 guidance calls for 170,000 to 185,000 deliveries, implying 20% plus full-year growth, supported by our Apex T Supercharged edition launch and Europe expansion.

Before we move on, let me provide our forward-looking revenue guidance for Q4 2024 and full fiscal year 2025, grounded in the strong momentum across vehicle production ramps, software growth, and energy business expansion.

For Q4, we are guiding revenue to $2.55 billion to $2.75 billion, representing approximately 25% to 35% sequential growth from Q3's $2.1 billion. This assumes average vehicle deliveries of 95,000 to 105,000 units, with an ASP of around $48,000 to $50,000, reflecting a richer mix toward our higher-margin Apex T pickup and Apex S/X refreshes. Automotive revenue should hit $2.35 billion to $2.50 billion, driven by our Austin Gigafactory operating at over 85% of its capacity target, thanks to 4680 structural battery packs reducing cell-to-pack costs by 18% quarter-over-quarter.

A key tailwind is our Full Self-Driving Supervised software adoption at 28% attach rate on new deliveries—up from 22% in Q2—contributing $150 million to $200 million in high-margin recurring revenue at over 85% gross margin. Early traction in Energy includes Megapack deployments accelerating to 2.5 GWh, generating $200 million at 45% margins, bolstered by our Lathrop Megafactory amid grid-scale storage demand from utilities.

Regionally, North America accounts for 70% of Q4 deliveries, fueled by IRA credits averaging $7,500 per vehicle. Europe at 20% faces 16% tariffs on Chinese cells, but we're mitigating with localized 4680 production at Berlin. In China, our Shanghai plant ramps exports to APAC.

Gross margins for Q4 should expand to 21% to 23%, up from 19% in Q3, as gigacasting cuts body-in-white costs by 30% and fixed-cost leverage from 20% production increase kicks in.

For full-year 2025, we expect total revenue of $12.8 billion to $13.8 billion, a 45% to 60% increase from 2024's $8.8 billion outlook. This implies Q1 2025 revenue of $3.0 billion to $3.2 billion. Vehicle deliveries projected at 450,000 to 480,000 units, with ASPs at $49,000 to $51,000 as we launch the refreshed Apex S and begin Apex T RWD production at $55,000, offering 400-plus mile range on 800V architecture.

Software and services scale to $1.2 billion to $1.5 billion, or 10% of revenue, with FSD v13 enabling Robotaxi beta by mid-year. Energy guided to $1.5 billion to $1.8 billion, with 12 GWh Megapack deployments capitalizing on global incentives.

We're prioritizing vertical integration against Chinese OEMs, with in-house Dojo training slashing inference costs by 40%. Cost discipline targets $2,500 per vehicle reductions through silicon carbide localization and recycled materials, aiming for 25% plus automotive gross margins.

Risks include semiconductor tightness and Europe subsidy phase-outs, but upside from Robotaxi or fleet wins. This reflects confidence outpacing industry growth.

I'll now turn the call over to Taylor Kim to provide an update on our manufacturing operations.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. We are pleased with the progress we've made in scaling up production of our key models like the Apex X and Apex T. Today, I'd like to dive into our factory expansions and operational efficiency improvements, which have been pivotal in driving our record delivery numbers—up 28% year-over-year to 185,000 vehicles in recent ramps—and expanding gross margins to 24.7%, our highest in three quarters. These are core to positioning Apex EV to capture accelerating EV demand projected at 17 million global units in 2025, while navigating Europe softening and supply chain volatility.

We've invested $2.8 billion in CapEx year-to-date, with 65% to capacity buildout—a step up from $1.9 billion in FY2023—to support 1.2 million annual production by end-2025, a 60% increase.

Flagship is Phase 2 of Nevada Gigafactory, our 5 million square foot facility optimized for 800V platforms. We've added lines for Apex S sedan and Apex C1 SUV, boosting cell-to-pack throughput by 40% to 120 GWh annually. Now at 85% capacity, full ramp by Q1 2025 supports IRA credits—we've claimed $450 million year-to-date.

In Europe, Brandenburg plant expansion for 300,000 units tailors to Battery Regulation, with Phase 1 at 15,000 units on Euro-spec models using Northvolt JV LFP. Targeting 98% localized BOM to sidestep CBAM tariffs, secured €1.2 billion subsidies.

In Asia, Shanghai JV with CATL scales to 80 GWh, $1.1 billion add-on for cylindrical cells, reducing import reliance by 35% amid price wars and U.S. tariffs. Output up 55% year-over-year.

Factories support multi-model flexibility with 48-hour SKU switches and 1,200-plus Giga Press units, slashing parts from 70 to 3 and die-change times by 70%.

On operational efficiency, we've delivered $620 million in OpEx savings year-to-date—12% ahead—pushing OEE to 92% from 81%. Automation via Siemens NX digital twins simulates 95% scenarios, cutting downtime 22%. Robotics at 1,850 per 100k sq ft handles 75% welding, 60% battery assembly. AI predictive maintenance via Palantir cuts stops 40%, saving $150 million.

Battery vertical integration yields 98.5%, dry electrode tech drops COGS 18% to $85/kWh below benchmarks. Supply chain onshoring 65% critical minerals cuts volatility. Labor efficiency up 32% to 45 vehicles per employee-shift via "Lights Out" pilots.

These shaved COGS 9.2% to $32,400 per vehicle, EBITDA margins up 420 bps to 16.8%. Our $1.45k EV per unit CapEx edges peers. Q4 CapEx moderates to $600 million, exiting at 950k run rate with headroom.

Risks like strikes mitigated by 18-month breakeven and 2.5x ROI. We're architecting a lean EV powerhouse.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for the Q&A session.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Please state your name and company when prompted.

Analyst 1:
Hi, this is Mike from Goldman Sachs. Great quarter on deliveries. Can you elaborate on the strategic priorities for Q4 and FY2025, especially production ramp and geographic expansion risks?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Mike. As we wrap up this strong quarter—delivering 152,000 vehicles up 28% year-over-year with gross margins at 24.8%—we're laser-focused on our "Scale, Innovate, Dominate" framework in the evolving EV market, where global penetration hit 18%. Our four pillars: Production Ramp to 500k run rate by YE2025, with Nevada at 85% utilization, Q4 targeting 32,000 deliveries on holiday demand and IRA rebates; FY25 capex $2.8B, 60% to Georgia Gigafactory 2 ramping 200k units, via 4680 integration slashing costs 25% to $65/kWh, Panasonic JV in Korea, inventory down to 45 days.

Product Pipeline: Q4 Apex C1 at $32,900, 320-mile range, 45k pre-orders; 2025 S refresh 800V, T1 truck teaser $45k 450-mile; 40% mix <$40k, software at 65% uptake $150 ARPU, FY25 $300M recurring.

Geographic: NA 75% revenue, dealer to 250; Europe pilot 2k C1, homologation Q1 for 50k sales; SEA JV Q2, China badge-engineered at $25k for 30k units; mix to 65/20/10/5 NA/EU/Asia/Emerging.

Tech Leadership: $500M R&D solid-state with QuantumScape, V2G standard, NVIDIA AI for 15% yields, 100% renewables by 2026.

Risks like metal prices, EU demand, competition mitigated by $1.2B cash, dynamic pricing ASP $48,500, backlog. Q4 sets FY25 $8.5-9.5B revenue, FCF positive H2, 1M run rate 2027.

Analyst 2:
Thanks. Emily from Morgan Stanley here. On revenue guidance, how does the Energy segment factor in, and any updates on software attach rates?

Jordan Lee:
Hi Emily. Energy accelerates with 2.5 GWh Megapacks in Q4 for $200M at 45% margins, scaling to $1.5-1.8B in 2025 on 12 GWh. Software at 28% attach, $150-200M Q4, scaling to $1.2-1.5B FY25 with Robotaxi beta. Guidance solid amid regional tailwinds like IRA, mitigations for tariffs.

Analyst 3:
Good morning, Raj from JPMorgan. Taylor, details on factory OEE gains and battery vertical integration progress?

Taylor Kim:
Thanks Raj. OEE at 92% via digital twins reducing downtime 22%, robotics 1,850 density, AI maintenance saving $150M. In-house packs 98.5% yield, 280 Wh/kg, $85/kWh COGS; Nevada 120 GWh throughput, Shanghai 80 GWh. Localization cuts freight 15%, labor 32% up. On track for efficiencies.

Analyst 4:
Hi, Lisa from Barclays. Alex, on cost reductions—BOM down 17% to $28,500—effectiveness across regions and FY25 targets?

Alex Rivera:
Lisa, spot on. Q3 BOM $28,500, 17% YoY cut, 450 bps margin expansion to 25.7%. Pillars: supply localization 25% lithium domestic saving $1,200/pack, logistics 22% down; gigacasting 50% structural cut, ABB automation 99.2% yields; 4680 at 50 GWh $72/kWh BladePlus, SiC powertrain 35% off; SG&A 320 bps to 7.8%. 92% savings realized, EBITDA +510 bps to 12.4%. NA 20% cut, Europe 14%, APAC 25%; FY24 15-18% further to $25k BOM, 30% margins. Scale yields 3-4% deflation per 10% volume.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for one more.

Analyst 5:
David from Citi. Jordan, risks to FY25 guidance like semis or subsidies, and cost savings ROI?

Jordan Lee:
David, semis mitigated by multi-sourcing TSMC/Samsung; Europe subsidies via localization. Costs 12:1 ROI on $70M capex, $850M YTD supply savings; overall $5.2B annualized. Upside Robotaxi/fleets. Confident in execution.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Apex EV Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
